slides.heading: Single Cycle Check
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Graphs
slides.narration: Let's solve Single Cycle Check, a medium graphs problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Do the jumps form one cycle visiting every index exactly once and returning to the start?
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Each element is a jump (wrapping). Do the jumps form one cycle visiting every index exactly once and returning to the start?

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Follow the jumps n times: we must visit every index exactly once and return to the start.
slides.narration: Follow the jumps n times: we must visit every index exactly once and return to the start.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Count jumps instead: n jumps, no early return to 0 → O(1) space
slides.narration: A visited array works but uses extra space. Counting is enough: if we make n jumps, never land on index zero early, and end at zero, every index was visited exactly once.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. If we return to zero early, fail
3. After n jumps we must be at zero
slides.narration: Step by step. First, jump n times with wrap-around. Second, if we return to zero early, fail. Third, after n jumps we must be at zero.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.narration: From index 0, jump 2 to index 2, wrapping around if needed.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.narration: From index 2, jump 1 to index 3, wrapping around if needed.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.narration: From index 3, jump -4 to index 5, wrapping around if needed.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.narration: From index 1, jump 3 to index 4, wrapping around if needed.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.narration: From index 4, jump -4 to index 0, wrapping around if needed.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: After 6 jumps we're back at 0 → single cycle
slides.narration: After exactly 6 jumps, we're back at index zero, and we never returned early. It's a single cycle.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We loop n times. If we land back on zero after at least one jump but before n jumps, we return false. Each step moves the index by the value with floor mod. Finally we check we're at zero.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Use floor mod so negative jumps wrap correctly, and remember that returning to zero too early means a smaller cycle.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Explain why n jumps + end at 0 suffices
Follow-up: detect any cycle from any start
slides.narration: Explain the counting argument carefully; that's what interviewers look for.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Follow the jumps n times: we must visit every index exactly once and return to the start.
slides.narration: To recap Single Cycle Check: Follow the jumps n times: we must visit every index exactly once and return to the start. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
